Alicia — thanks for the clear framing. Short answer: yes, we can propose a limited indexation approach. I attached a mutual action plan (MA) and a simple pricing workbook with three options: fixed-rate, capped indexation, and a blended-rate with a 12-month reprice window.

High-level tradeoffs:
- Fixed-rate = best predictability for you, more exposure for us if GPU market drops.
- Capped indexation = shared upside/downside within a bounded band (e.g., +/-10% annual).
- Blended with reprice = initial fixed discount for commit term, then 12-month review tied to a published GPU cost index (we reference the Redwood GPU Spot Index + vendor MSRP).

Action items: can you confirm which option Rajiv prefers? If capped indexation, we need legal + finance approval for the cap levels. Looping in Marissa for finance sensitivity and Karthik for pricing guardrails.

Steph — quick internal note before we reply to customer. I ran three scenarios in the workbook: conservative (GPU downturn), base (flat), and bullish (GPU cost rise). Key observations:
1) For a 12-month, $120k/mo reserved pool, a +/-10% band on indexation changes Redwood margin by ~6–8% depending on amortization of reserved infra.
2) A cap of +/-7% keeps margin impact within our internal reserve tolerance for standard enterprise deals. Anything looser needs an escalation to Ben (re risk exceptions).
3) Blended reprice with a 12-month floor (no downward rebate <3%) is viable to protect our ability to average across customer mix.

Recommend: offer capped indexation band +/-7% with a hard floor of -3% on downward adjustments for the first 12 months; also include option to renegotiate at year 2 if market variance exceeds 15% cumulative. This is defensible to finance and gives the client some downside protection.

Marissa
Dir, Finance — Pricing

Alicia / Rajiv — appreciative of the patience while we reviewed. Attached is an updated MA and the pricing worksheet reflecting the internal guidance:

Proposal summary (short):
- Commit term: 12 months reserved pool (option to extend to 24 months).
- Pricing: two tranches — 70% fixed-rate at agreed rate; 30% indexed with a capped band of +/-7% per 12-month period.
- Downward protection: no downward adjustment >3% during first 12 months.
- Renegotiation trigger: if cumulative market movement >15% over a rolling 12-month period, either party can request reprice discussions; changes require mutual agreement.
- Upside credit: for commitments >=2x current monthly usage, a one-time signing credit equal to 3% of first-year committed spend applied to month 2 invoice.

If this aligns with your budget windows, we can surface a redline for legal next week. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the workbook assumptions.

Thanks,
